calibration.reason: Clear labels and a familiar layout support the task, but the misplaced focus after invalid input is a material usability flaw.

primary_action.input: Tab to the selected 4 m radio, then ArrowRight.
primary_action.expected: Select 6 m and show all three closures.
primary_action.observed: 6 m was selected; the list showed Riverside path closes, Ferry stops, and Footbridge closes.

A-1440.edge_observation: Two ArrowLeft presses selected 2 m and the list contained only Riverside path closes.
A-1440.fact_check: At 6 m the drawn waterline aligned with the 6 m gauge mark and the text. Actual local closure thresholds and live river conditions are unsupported by the view.
A-1440.strength: The large cross-section, gauge marks and closure list form a clear, unified explanation.
A-1440.weakness: The drawing does not label the path, ferry and bridge directly, so the reader must infer which feature corresponds to each closure.
A-1440.repair: Add concise labels to the illustrated crossings while preserving the uncluttered scale.

primary_action.expected: Select 6 m and show all three closures.
primary_action.observed: 6 m was selected and all three closures appeared.

A-390.edge_observation: Two ArrowLeft presses selected 2 m; only Riverside path closes remained in the list.
A-390.fact_check: The visible waterline aligned with the 6 m mark and the 6 m text. Actual local conditions and thresholds are unsupported.
A-390.strength: The illustration, control and closure list fit together in the initial mobile viewport, with a clear keyboard focus outline.
A-390.weakness: The reduced diagram makes crossing details and gauge labels small.
A-390.repair: Improve small-screen diagram labeling and legibility without pushing the controls far below the illustration.

primary_action.input: Tab through the slider and closure rows to the 6 m footbridge row, then Enter.
primary_action.expected: Set 6 m and show the path and footbridge closed and the ferry stopped.
primary_action.observed: The level changed to 6 m, all three rows showed closure states, and the status reported 3 of 3 levels reached.

B-1440.edge_observation: Two Shift+Tab presses and Enter set 2 m. Only the path was marked closed, but the list still included the ferry and footbridge as 'Level not reached'.
B-1440.fact_check: At 6 m the waterline aligned with the diagram's 6 m mark and the text. Actual local conditions and thresholds are unsupported.
B-1440.strength: Direct labels on the cross-section connect each crossing to its elevation, and closure rows can act as keyboard shortcuts.
B-1440.weakness: The rows look primarily like status information, so their ability to set a level is not visually obvious; the 2 m list also does not contain only the path.
B-1440.repair: Make the row action explicit and separate reached closures from upcoming thresholds.

primary_action.input: Tab through the slider and closure rows to the 6 m footbridge row, then Enter.
primary_action.expected: Set 6 m and show all three closure states.
primary_action.observed: The level changed to 6 m and all three rows showed the expected closed or stopped states.

B-390.edge_observation: Two Shift+Tab presses and Enter set 2 m. The path alone was marked closed; the ferry and footbridge remained listed as 'Level not reached'.
B-390.fact_check: The drawn waterline aligned with 6 m and the displayed value. Actual local conditions and thresholds are unsupported.
B-390.strength: The labeled cross-section and all three status rows remain visible in the mobile viewport.
B-390.weakness: Diagram labels become small, and the status rows' function as level-setting buttons is not apparent before interaction.
B-390.repair: Increase diagram label legibility and signal that each threshold row can be activated; distinguish current closures from unreached levels.

preference.reason: Both views successfully reached 6 m and visually matched the waterline to the value. A makes its level choices explicit and meets the requested 2 m list behavior, while B keeps unreached crossings in the closure list and hides its useful row shortcuts behind status-like presentation.

decision: Round 2 still beat stock, but fell below River round 1 on desktop and tied on mobile. Retain round 1 as the strongest verified river draft. Try directly labeled contours in round 3.
